reports.title: THE TJX COMPANIES, INC. REPORTS Q3 FY27 RESULTS; COMP SALES GROWTH OF 4%, PRETAX PROFIT MARGIN, AND DILUTED EARNINGS PER SHARE ALL ABOVE PLAN

lines: The Company now expects to repurchase approximately $3.0 billion of TJX stock during Fiscal 2027.
For the full year Fiscal 2027, the Company now expects consolidated comparable sales to be up 4%.
The Company expects its full-year pretax profit margin to be 12.4%.

Excluding an expected net benefit of 0.3 to 0.4 percentage points from tariff refunds, the Company continues to expect its full-year adjusted pretax profit margin to be in the range of 12.0% to 12.1%.
The Company expects its full-year diluted earnings per share outlook to be in the range of $5.33 to $5.36.
Excluding an expected net benefit of $.16 from tariff refunds, the Company expects its full year outlook for adjusted diluted earnings per share to be in the range of $5.17 to $5.20.

desk.headline: Sales up 6% to $16.0bn, beat; full-year EPS range tightened upward, Q4 margin trimmed for fuel
results: Net sales rose 6% to $16.0bn and comparable sales grew 4%, ahead of the company's own plan.
Growth was led by TJX International (comps +8%), TJX Canada (+6%) and HomeGoods (+5%); the main Marmaxx chain improved to +2%.
Adjusted EPS rose 5% to $1.34; reported EPS of $1.39 includes a $0.05 net gain from US tariff refunds.
Adjusted gross margin fell 0.5 points to 32.1% on higher freight and fuel costs, partly offset by lower SG&A.
Store count rose by 64 to 5,349; the company repaid a $1.0bn note and returned $1.5bn to shareholders.

guidance.summary: Full-year comp growth is now 4% (was 3–4%) and the adjusted EPS range moved up at the low end to $5.17–5.20. Q4 calls for comps of 2–3% and adjusted EPS of $1.42–1.45, with extra fuel costs now assumed.

points: Marmaxx improved through the quarter in both apparel and home; management sees its few execution issues largely fixed by year-end.
Unusually warm weather in the US and Canada has held back some categories early in Q4, but holiday sales are expected to build.
Freight and fuel are the biggest margin headwind; Q4 adjusted gross margin is guided down 0.5–0.6 points.
Q4 guidance assumes no further tariff refunds; full-year adjusted pretax margin target was kept despite the fuel pressure.
Long-term goal remains 7,500 stores, with store growth planned to speed up to about 4% a year from next year.
call.source: Q3 FY27 call transcript — The Motley Fool, 18 Nov 2026; prior outlook from the Q2 FY27 release (19 Aug 2026)

watch: Whether Marmaxx comps keep improving through the holiday season.
Freight and fuel costs versus the lower Q4 gross margin plan.
